assessment: Assessment and late submission guidance. Students should upload coursework through the learning portal before the deadline shown on the course page. The final submission must be a readable PDF unless the instructor has approved another format in writing. Students should open the uploaded file after submission and confirm that the correct version is visible. A submission receipt should be saved until the grade is released. Late submission is normally penalized according to the assessment schedule. Illness extensions require medical evidence before the deadline. A student who becomes ill should contact the course coordinator as early as possible and provide the required evidence before the original deadline; the exception does not automatically approve an extension. A request made after the deadline may be reviewed only under the published exceptional-circumstances process. Internet problems do not automatically remove the penalty, so students should not wait until the final minutes to upload. Group work must identify all group members on the cover page. Students must not submit another student's work as their own. If the portal displays an error, take a screenshot without exposing passwords and contact the help desk. Keep the assignment file and receipt until the result is confirmed. The coordinator is responsible for confirming an approved extension and its revised date.
it_help: Account access and password recovery guidance. A forgotten password can be reset using the recovery link on the university login page. Enter the registered email address and follow the instructions sent to that mailbox. If the message does not arrive, check the spam folder and confirm that the registered address is still accessible. Never share a password or recovery code with another person, including someone claiming to be support staff. Recovery codes are private credentials and must not be printed in logs or pasted into public chat. If the account is locked after repeated attempts, wait for the stated lock period or contact the IT help desk for identity verification. The help desk may ask for a student ID through its official secure channel, but it will never ask for the current password. Multi-factor authentication should remain enabled. If a phone used for authentication is lost, report the loss through the official support route so the account owner can be verified. Do not use a link from an unexpected message; open the university portal directly. A successful reset does not mean that suspicious account activity has been resolved. Report unexpected sign-in alerts to IT support. Staff will review the event and advise whether additional steps are needed.
returns: Parcel delivery and returns guidance. Customers should inspect a delivered parcel as soon as practical and keep the outer packaging until the item has been checked. For a damaged parcel, contact support within 48 hours and attach photographs of the item and packaging. The report should include the order reference and a short description of the damage. The 48-hour reporting window applies to the Pakistan service region in this synthetic example. A different regional guide may state a different reporting window; do not apply another region's rule to a Pakistan order. For a change of mind, return unused items within 14 days in their original packaging, subject to the listed product exclusions. A damaged item is handled through the damage-report process rather than the change-of-mind route. Support may request additional photographs if the damage is not clear. Do not discard packaging before support confirms that it is no longer required. Refund or replacement decisions are made after the evidence is reviewed and are not guaranteed merely because a report was submitted. Keep the support case number for follow-up. If the parcel is missing rather than damaged, use the delivery investigation form instead of the damage form. This is synthetic teaching content and is not an actual retailer policy.
workplace: Remote work and workplace access guidance. Employees may request remote work with manager approval, subject to role requirements and the team's operational needs. Approval should be recorded through the normal workplace process before a remote arrangement begins. Contractors are different from employees for this rule. Contractors may work remotely only when the signed contract explicitly permits remote work. A manager's informal verbal agreement does not replace the signed contract condition. Employee remote-work rules must not be assumed to apply to contractors. If a contract is silent about remote work, the contractor should ask the contract owner for written clarification before working remotely. Access to internal systems must follow the user's approved role and security requirements regardless of work location. Public Wi-Fi should not be used for sensitive work unless the approved secure connection is active. Staff should lock their devices when away from the desk and report lost equipment promptly. Remote access can be suspended if a security concern is being investigated. This example is a synthetic workplace policy, not legal or employment advice. A real organization must check the current signed agreement and current policy owner before making a decision. Policy versions and effective dates should be recorded when this guidance is adapted.
equipment: Printer and office equipment troubleshooting guidance. Before troubleshooting, check that the printer is powered on, connected to the correct computer or network, and showing no warning light that requires service. For blank printer pages: 1. Check ink or toner level. 2. Run the printer cleaning utility from the device software. 3. Print a test page and inspect whether text is visible. Follow the device manual because menu names differ between models. Do not open a hot printer assembly or touch electrical components. If the printer reports a paper jam, switch it off using the normal power control and follow the model-specific paper removal instructions. A blank scanner image is a different problem: check document placement and select the correct scanning source. Do not apply scanner instructions to a printer fault simply because both produce blank output. If the cleaning utility does not help, check whether the protective tape was removed from a new cartridge and verify that the selected paper type is supported. Record the printer model and error message before contacting technical support. Repeated cleaning cycles can waste ink, so stop if the manual recommends service. These instructions are synthetic and should be checked against the actual device manual.
